美国酸雨计划为什么常被当作排污权交易成功的教科书案例？

Why is the U.S. Acid Rain Program cited as the textbook success of emissions trading?

1990 年《清洁空气法》修正案第四篇为发电厂二氧化硫设定总量上限，并允许配额自由买卖，同时强制安装连续排放监测系统以保证数据可信。电厂据此自主选择低硫煤、洗涤塔或购买配额，减排集中发生在成本最低的机组，全国二氧化硫排放到 2020 年比 1990 年下降九成以上。事后评估显示实际履约成本远低于立法时的预测，健康效益与成本之比达到数十倍，这一经验直接影响了后来欧盟碳市场的设计。
Title IV of the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments capped power-plant sulphur dioxide, let allowances trade freely, and mandated continuous emission monitoring so the data could be trusted. Utilities chose among low-sulphur coal, scrubbers, or buying allowances, concentrating abatement where it was cheapest, and national SO2 emissions fell by more than 90% between 1990 and 2020. Retrospective analyses found compliance costs far below legislative forecasts and health benefits exceeding costs by an order of magnitude or more, lessons that shaped the later design of the EU carbon market.

欧盟碳边境调节机制如何运作？它试图解决什么问题？

How does the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism work, and what problem is it meant to solve?

碳边境调节机制要求进口水泥、钢铁、铝、化肥、电力和氢等产品的申报人报告产品的隐含碳排放，并按欧盟排放交易体系的价格补缴差额，同时可扣除在原产国已支付的碳价。2023 至 2025 年为只报告不缴费的过渡期，2026 年起进入正式征收阶段，并与欧盟内部免费配额的退坡同步。其目标是防止碳泄漏，即在欧盟内部碳价上升时，高排放生产环节转移到监管宽松的国家，反而抬高全球排放。
The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism obliges declarants importing cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, and hydrogen to report the embedded emissions of those goods and pay the difference against the EU Emissions Trading System price, with credit for any carbon price already paid abroad. A transitional reporting-only phase runs from 2023 to 2025, with financial obligations starting in 2026 and phased in as free allocation inside the EU is withdrawn. The aim is to prevent carbon leakage, whereby a rising internal carbon price pushes emissions-intensive production to laxly regulated countries and raises global emissions.

自然相关财务披露（TNFD）是什么？

What is the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD)?

TNFD是一套帮助企业评估和披露其运营对自然依赖与影响的框架，类似气候领域的TCFD。它推动资金流向对自然友好的活动，降低生态退化带来的金融风险。越来越多企业正据此报告生物多样性相关风险。
The TNFD is a framework helping companies assess and disclose their dependencies on and impacts on nature, analogous to the climate-focused TCFD. It steers finance toward nature-positive activities and reduces financial risks from ecological decline. A growing number of firms report biodiversity risks under it.

欧盟碳排放交易体系（EU ETS）是如何运作的？

How does the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) work?

EU ETS是全球最大的碳市场，对电力、工业等行业的排放设定逐年下降的总量上限。企业须持有与排放相等的配额，超额可从市场购买，剩余可出售。其限额与交易机制已推动欧盟减排并影响全球碳定价。
The EU ETS is the world's largest carbon market, capping emissions from power, industry, and other sectors with a declining total limit. Firms must hold allowances equal to their emissions, buying shortfalls and selling surpluses in the market. Its cap-and-trade design has driven EU reductions and influenced global carbon pricing.

实证研究对碳泄漏的规模给出了什么结论？

What does empirical research conclude about the actual scale of carbon leakage?

理论上单边碳约束会让高排放产业外移，但计量研究发现现实中的泄漏率通常低于产业界的预警。对《京都议定书》时期贸易流的分析显示，承担减排义务的国家进口品的隐含碳强度上升，存在可测的泄漏，但规模只相当于其减排量的一小部分。原因是能源成本在多数制造业成本中占比有限，选址还取决于劳动力、市场距离和基础设施，只有铝、水泥等少数电力或排放密集行业风险显著，这也是边境调节主要针对这些品类的原因。
Theory predicts unilateral carbon constraints will push emissions-intensive production abroad, but econometric work finds real-world leakage rates generally below industry warnings. Analyses of trade flows during the Kyoto period show the embodied carbon intensity of imports into committed countries rose, indicating measurable leakage, yet only a modest fraction of the abatement achieved. Energy costs are a limited share of most manufacturing costs and location also depends on labour, market proximity, and infrastructure, so significant exposure is concentrated in electricity- or emissions-intensive sectors such as aluminium and cement — precisely the products border adjustment targets.

什么是“生物多样性信贷”？它和碳信用有什么不同？

What are biodiversity credits, and how do they differ from carbon credits?

生物多样性信贷是为可验证的栖息地保护或恢复成果发放的凭证。企业购买这类信贷，用以支持自身的自然向好承诺。与碳信用不同，生物多样性缺乏统一的全球换算单位，保护成果难以标准化测量，因此这类信贷通常不允许交易或用于抵消。购买它意味着额外出资创造保护增益，而不是买破坏权，目前这类信贷主要在自愿市场试点。
Biodiversity credits are certificates issued for verifiable habitat protection or restoration outcomes. Companies buy them to back their own nature-positive pledges. Unlike carbon, biodiversity lacks a unified global accounting unit and outcomes are hard to standardise, so such credits are generally non-tradable and non-offsettable. Buying them means funding additional conservation gains rather than purchasing a right to harm; these credits are currently piloted in voluntary markets.

碳税和碳市场有什么不同？为什么都是“给碳定价”？

How do a carbon tax and a carbon market differ, and why are both forms of pricing carbon?

两者都让排放二氧化碳变得有成本。碳税直接按每吨排放定价，价格稳定、执行简单，但总排放量难以事先锁定；碳市场（总量控制与交易）先设总排放上限再发放配额，配额可在企业间交易，总量可控但价格随行就市。许多经济体同时使用两者，并逐步提高碳价，以引导资金流向低碳技术。
Both put a price on emitting CO2. A carbon tax charges a fixed rate per tonne — the price is stable and administration is simple, but total emissions are not capped in advance. A carbon market (cap-and-trade) sets a total cap and issues allowances that firms can buy and sell, so emissions are capped while the price floats. Many economies use both and ratchet prices up over time to steer investment toward low-carbon technology.

什么是“污染者付费”原则？

What is the polluter pays principle?

“污染者付费”原则要求造成污染的一方承担治理和赔偿的费用，而不是由公众或政府买单。它用经济手段倒逼企业减少排放、采用清洁技术。这一原则被许多国际环境公约和各国法律所采纳。
The polluter pays principle requires those who cause pollution to bear the cost of cleanup and compensation, not the public or government. It uses economic pressure to make firms cut emissions and adopt clean technology. Many international accords and national laws adopt it.

ESG评分和绿色债券如何真正影响环境？又有什么风险？

How do ESG ratings and green bonds actually affect the environment, and what are the risks?

ESG评价把环境、社会与治理因素纳入投资决策，理论上会推高高污染项目的融资成本。绿色债券则把募集资金锁定到明确的绿色项目，并通常附带报告义务。但两者的实际环境影响取决于标准质量和漂绿风险。如果评分体系彼此不一致，或者绿色资金流向灰色项目，效果就会大打折扣，因此监管正在统一绿色标签和核查机制。
ESG rating folds environmental, social, and governance factors into investment decisions and, in theory, raises financing costs for polluting projects. Green bonds earmark proceeds to defined green projects and usually come with reporting obligations. But the actual environmental impact of both depends on standards quality and greenwashing risk. If rating systems are inconsistent or green money flows to grey projects, the effect weakens — which is why regulators are harmonising green labels and verification.

生态修复能让退化生态系统“恢复原样”吗？

Can ecological restoration bring a degraded ecosystem back to its original state?

生态修复通过植树、退耕还林还草、河流自然化、矿山复绿等手段，帮助受损生态系统重建结构与功能，目标是恢复其自我维持能力，而非简单种回去。但修复周期以十年计、成本高昂，且几乎无法完全还原原始生态。因此生态学强调预防优于修复：保住完好的生态系统，永远是最合算的投资。
Ecological restoration rebuilds structure and function in damaged ecosystems — replanting, returning farmland to forest or grassland, re-naturalising rivers and greening mines — aiming for self-sustaining systems rather than simply replanting the original vegetation. Yet restoration takes decades and costs far more than prevention, and it can rarely recreate the original ecosystem. Ecologists therefore stress prevention over repair: protecting intact ecosystems is always the better investment.

企业的“净零承诺”如何避免沦为空洞口号？

How can corporate net-zero commitments avoid becoming empty slogans?

可信的净零承诺要符合1.5°C对齐框架。企业应设定经科学验证的短期与长期目标，例如通过SBTi的验证。企业还应优先削减自身价值链的排放，把抵消严格限制在剩余排放范围内，并公开年度进展。同时承诺必须覆盖范围1、2、3的全部排放，而不是只挑容易核算的部分，研究与监管也正在共同打击零碳夸大行为。
A credible net-zero commitment must follow a 1.5°C-aligned framework. Companies should set science-based near- and long-term targets, for example validated by SBTi. They should prioritise cutting value-chain emissions, strictly limit offsets to residual emissions, and publish annual progress. Commitments must also cover all Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions rather than cherry-picking the easy parts, and research and regulation are jointly cracking down on zero-washing.

What is the significance of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework's '30×30' target?

「30×30」目标要求到 2030 年保护至少 30% 的陆地和海洋区域。它是 2022 年联合国生物多样性公约通过、具里程碑意义的框架核心，并配套了资源调动与生物多样性主流化指标。
The '30×30' target aims to protect at least 30% of land and sea by 2030. Adopted in 2022 under the CBD, it is the centerpiece of a landmark framework backed by financing and mainstreaming indicators.

什么是生产者责任延伸（EPR）？

What is extended producer responsibility (EPR)?

生产者责任延伸要求制造商对其产品从设计、生产到使用后的回收处理全过程负责，而不仅是销售环节。它促使企业设计更易回收、更耐用的产品，并出资建设回收体系。电子电器和包装物常是EPR的重点对象。
Extended producer responsibility makes manufacturers accountable for their products across design, production, and end-of-life recycling, not just sale. It pushes firms to design durable, recyclable goods and fund collection systems. Electronics and packaging are common EPR targets.

环境库兹涅茨曲线为什么不能被当作经济增长自动改善环境的证据？

Why can't the environmental Kuznets curve be read as proof that growth automatically cleans the environment?

该假说认为污染随人均收入先升后降，呈倒 U 形，最早的实证来自跨国截面数据中二氧化硫与颗粒物的表现。质疑有三层：倒 U 形主要出现在有明确健康危害、治理成本较低的局地污染物，二氧化碳和生物多样性损失并未显现类似拐点；下降往往由污染密集产业外移和进口替代造成，是空间转移而非总量改善；截面回归还容易混淆国家间差异与单国时间路径。因此曲线更像是政策与制度作用的结果，而非收入增长的自动结果。
The hypothesis holds that pollution rises then falls with income per capita in an inverted U, with early evidence drawn from cross-country data on sulphur dioxide and particulates. Three objections stand out: the inverted U appears mainly for local pollutants with clear health damage and cheap abatement, while carbon dioxide and biodiversity loss show no comparable turning point; declines often stem from relocating dirty industry and importing the goods instead, a spatial shift rather than a real reduction; and cross-sectional regressions conflate differences between countries with the trajectory of any single one. The curve is better read as the imprint of policy and institutions than as an automatic dividend of growth.

20世纪60年代蕾切尔·卡逊《寂静的春天》的出版对美国现代环境主义运动起到了怎样的催化作用?

How did the 1962 publication of Rachel Carson's Silent Spring catalyze the modern American environmental movement?

该书系统揭露了滴滴涕等持久性有机氯农药沿食物链富集、导致鸟类种群锐减的证据,首次把生态毒理学推向公众视野。它直接推动了1970年美国环保署的设立和1972年联邦对滴滴涕的禁用,并被视为美国现代环境立法浪潮的思想起点。
The book marshaled evidence that persistent organochlorine pesticides such as DDT bioaccumulated along food chains and devastated bird populations, bringing ecotoxicology into public view for the first time. It directly contributed to the creation of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in 1970 and the federal DDT ban of 1972, and is regarded as an intellectual starting point for the wave of modern U.S. environmental legislation.

为什么仅对单个建设项目做环评不足以保障区域环境质量？规划环评（战略性环境评价）在机制上如何弥补这一缺口？

Why can project-by-project environmental impact assessment fail to safeguard regional environmental quality, and how does plan-level strategic environmental assessment close this gap?

项目环评把现状本底当作固定背景，单个项目逐案达标，多个项目的排放与扰动却在区域尺度上叠加，形成累积效应导致“合规而恶化”。规划环评将评价前移到土地利用与产业布局阶段，通过方案比选核查区域总量与环境承载力，从源头调整或否决会累积超载的规划，再向单个项目分配总量指标，避免锁定不可逆退化。
Project EIA treats existing conditions as fixed background, so each development can comply case by case while their combined emissions and disturbances still accumulate regionally — compliance yet deterioration. Plan-level assessment moves evaluation upstream to land-use and industrial-layout decisions: alternatives are tested against regional totals and carrying capacity, overloaded plans are adjusted or rejected at source, and budgets are then allocated downward to individual projects.

什么是气候正义？

What is climate justice?

气候正义强调应对气候变化时须兼顾公平：排放少的发展中国家与未来世代却承受最严重后果。它要求历史排放大国承担更多责任并提供资金技术支持。正义维度把道德与权利纳入气候政策核心。
Climate justice stresses fairness in climate response: those who emitted least—developing countries and future generations—often bear the worst consequences. It demands that major historical emitters take greater responsibility and provide finance and technology. The justice dimension puts ethics and rights at the core of climate policy.

《蒙特利尔议定书》基加利修正案为什么被称为一项气候协定？

Why is the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol described as a climate agreement?

氢氟碳化物是为替代破坏臭氧层的氟氯烃而推广的制冷剂，本身几乎不损耗臭氧，但增温潜势可达二氧化碳的数百到上万倍。2016 年通过的基加利修正案把这类物质纳入议定书管制，要求各国按分组时间表逐步削减生产与消费。联合国环境规划署估计，全面履约可在本世纪末避免最多约 0.4℃ 的升温，因此这项修正案实质上是用臭氧公约的成熟履约机制来完成气候减排任务。
Hydrofluorocarbons were adopted as refrigerants to replace ozone-depleting chlorofluorocarbons; they barely touch the ozone layer but have global warming potentials hundreds to tens of thousands of times that of carbon dioxide. The Kigali Amendment, adopted in 2016, brought them under the Protocol with staged phase-down schedules for production and consumption by country group. UNEP estimates full compliance could avoid up to about 0.4°C of warming by the end of the century, so the amendment effectively borrows the ozone treaty's proven compliance machinery to deliver climate mitigation.

碳排放交易市场是如何运作的？

How does an emissions trading system work?

政府先设定总排放上限并向企业分配或拍卖排放配额。企业若减排低于配额可出售余量，超标则需购买，从而以最低成本实现总量控制。配额逐年收紧以推动整体减排。
The government sets a total emission cap and allocates or auctions allowances to firms. Companies that emit below their allowance can sell the surplus, while those exceeding it must buy, achieving the cap at lowest cost. The cap is tightened over time to drive overall reductions.

全球碳定价机制已经覆盖多少排放？为什么价格水平差异如此之大？

How much of global emissions do carbon pricing schemes cover, and why do prices differ so much?

世界银行的年度评估显示，全球已运行数十项碳税与排放交易体系，合计覆盖约四分之一的温室气体排放，年度收入超过千亿美元。价格差异巨大：欧盟排放交易体系的配额价格长期在每吨数十欧元甚至接近百欧元，而一些以增加财政收入为主的碳税仅为每吨数美元。差异来自减排目标的严格程度、配额总量与免费分配比例、行业竞争力顾虑以及政治可接受度，因此覆盖率高并不等于约束力强。
The World Bank's annual review counts dozens of operating carbon taxes and emissions trading systems covering roughly a quarter of global greenhouse gas emissions and raising over a hundred billion dollars a year. Prices vary enormously: EU allowances have traded in the tens of euros and at times near a hundred, while some carbon taxes designed mainly to raise revenue sit at a few dollars per tonne. The spread reflects target stringency, cap levels and free allocation, competitiveness concerns, and political acceptability, so wide coverage does not automatically mean binding constraint.

企业为什么要披露碳排放等环境信息？

Why should companies disclose environmental information such as carbon emissions?

环境信息披露让投资者、消费者和监管者看清企业的气候风险与污染责任，帮助资金流向低碳转型。全球趋势正从自愿走向强制：ISSB国际准则和多数证券交易所的披露要求，使“碳数据”变得与财务报表同等重要，同时也倒逼企业设定减碳目标并真正落实。
Environmental disclosure lets investors, consumers, and regulators see corporate climate risk and pollution liabilities, steering capital toward the low-carbon transition. The global trend runs from voluntary to mandatory: ISSB standards and most stock-exchange requirements make carbon data as important as financial statements, and also push firms to set and actually deliver reduction targets.

什么是欧盟的“碳边境调节机制”（CBAM）？它想解决什么问题？

What is the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and what problem does it address?

CBAM（俗称碳关税）要求进口商为钢铁、水泥、铝、电力等高碳产品购买碳凭证，使其碳成本与欧盟内部碳价相当。它针对的是“碳泄漏”——企业把生产转移到碳约束宽松的国家，从而抵消欧盟内部的减排努力，同时也推动贸易伙伴建立自己的碳定价。
CBAM (commonly called a carbon tariff) requires importers to buy certificates for high-carbon goods such as steel, cement, aluminum, and electricity, aligning their carbon cost with the EU's internal carbon price. It targets carbon leakage — firms relocating production to jurisdictions with lax carbon constraints, which would offset EU domestic reductions — while also nudging trading partners to adopt carbon pricing of their own.

什么是“环境正义”？为什么污染设施常集中在弱势社区？

What is environmental justice, and why are polluting facilities often concentrated in disadvantaged communities?

环境正义关注环境负担与收益的分配是否公平：现实中，工业区、垃圾场和污染设施常选址在低收入和少数族裔社区，而绿地与洁净水又更集中在富裕社区，形成“环境不平等”。环境正义主张受影响社区参与决策、获得同等保护与合理补偿，如今已被写入多国的环境政策。
Environmental justice asks whether environmental burdens and benefits are fairly distributed: in practice, industrial zones, landfills, and polluting facilities often locate in low-income and minority communities while green space and clean water concentrate in wealthier ones — environmental inequality. It demands that affected communities take part in decisions and receive equal protection and fair compensation, and it is now embedded in many national policies.

“海绵城市”是靠什么来防内涝的？

What does a sponge city rely on to prevent urban flooding?

海绵城市让城市像海绵一样“吸水、蓄水、渗水、净水”：透水铺装让雨水就地入渗，雨水花园和绿色屋顶蓄存径流，湿地与蓄水池调蓄暴雨，再把净化后的水回用或补充地下水。通过把硬化地面恢复成可渗透的绿色设施，城市能削峰错峰、缓解内涝，同时改善水环境。
A sponge city lets urban areas absorb, store, infiltrate and purify rainwater like a sponge: permeable pavements let rain soak in where it falls, rain gardens and green roofs hold runoff, and wetlands and reservoirs regulate storms, while treated water is reused or recharges groundwater. By restoring hard surfaces to permeable, green infrastructure, cities flatten flood peaks, ease waterlogging and improve water quality.

“污染者付费”原则是什么意思？

What does the 'polluter pays' principle mean?

它要求造成污染或环境损害的一方承担治理和赔偿成本，而不是由公众买单。这是经合组织提出的环境政策基石，被用于排污收费、环境税和损害赔偿等设计。
It holds that whoever causes pollution or environmental damage should bear the cost of cleanup and compensation, not the public. Proposed by the OECD as a cornerstone of environmental policy, it underpins pollution charges, environmental taxes and liability rules.

个人生活里哪些行动减排效果最实在？

Which personal actions genuinely cut emissions the most?

科学评估显示，高影响行动包括减少红肉消费、少乘飞机多乘火车、选择步行骑行公交、住在节能房屋、购买高效率家电并延长物品使用寿命。这些行动比随手关灯这类小事的减排量高出许多。低碳生活不是做苦行僧，而是把有限的精力用在刀刃上，先改掉高排放的习惯。
Research-based rankings show the highest-impact individual actions include eating less red meat, flying less and taking trains more, choosing walking, cycling and transit, living in efficient housing, buying high-efficiency appliances and keeping goods in use longer. These dwarf the savings of small gestures like turning off lights. Low-carbon living is not about austerity — it is focusing effort on the habits that emit most.

共同但有区别的责任原则是什么？

What is the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities?

该原则承认所有国家都有应对气候变化的共同义务，但发达国家因历史排放更多、能力更强而应承担更大责任。它体现于《联合国气候变化框架公约》及后续协定。这一原则平衡了公平与全球行动效率。
The principle acknowledges all nations share the duty to address climate change, but developed countries, with greater historical emissions and capacity, should bear more responsibility. It is embedded in the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and later agreements. The principle balances equity with the efficiency of global action.

《全球甲烷承诺》承诺了什么？为什么油气行业被视为最容易的减排突破口？

What does the Global Methane Pledge commit to, and why is the oil and gas sector seen as the easiest win?

《全球甲烷承诺》在 2021 年格拉斯哥气候大会上发起，签署方承诺到 2030 年把全球人为甲烷排放相对 2020 年水平至少削减 30%，已有一百五十多个国家加入。油气行业之所以被看作突破口，是因为大量排放来自可修补的阀门泄漏、放空与不完全火炬燃烧，减排措施往往能靠回收的天然气收回成本。国际能源署估算，该行业约四成甲烷排放可以零净成本消除。
Launched at the Glasgow climate conference in 2021, the Global Methane Pledge commits signatories to cut collective anthropogenic methane emissions at least 30% below 2020 levels by 2030, and more than 150 countries have joined. Oil and gas is treated as the low-hanging fruit because much of its output comes from repairable valve leaks, venting, and incomplete flaring, where abatement often pays for itself through the recovered gas. The International Energy Agency estimates roughly 40% of the sector's methane emissions could be eliminated at no net cost.

What is the role of the Green Climate Fund (GCF)?

The GCF is a key financial mechanism under the Paris Agreement that helps developing countries fund mitigation and adaptation projects. Developed nations pledge contributions, and the fund supports clean energy, disaster preparedness, and more. It aims to close the climate finance gap and enable a just transition.

什么是碳排放权交易（碳市场）？

What is cap-and-trade (carbon market)?

碳排放权交易是政府先设定一个排放总量上限（cap），然后把排放配额分配给企业，允许排放少的企业把多余配额卖给超标的企业（trade）。它用市场机制以最低成本实现减排。欧盟碳排放交易体系是全球最大的碳市场。
Cap-and-trade sets an overall emission cap, allocates allowances to firms, and lets those under the limit sell surplus permits to those over it. It uses the market to cut emissions at lowest cost. The EU Emissions Trading System is the world's largest carbon market.

昆明-蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架的 30x30 目标具体要求什么？

What exactly does the 30x30 target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework require?

2022 年《生物多样性公约》第十五次缔约方大会通过的框架，其目标三要求到 2030 年有效保护和管理全球至少 30% 的陆地、内陆水域以及海洋与沿海区域。文本强调保护地网络应具有生态代表性、连通性和公平治理，并首次明确承认原住民与地方社区的传统领地和权利。与此前的爱知目标相比，30x30 更强调质量而非单纯面积，因为纸上公园式的保护地无法阻止实际的栖息地丧失。
Target 3 of the framework adopted at the fifteenth Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity in 2022 calls for effective conservation and management of at least 30% of terrestrial, inland water, coastal, and marine areas by 2030. The text stresses that protected area networks be ecologically representative, well connected, and equitably governed, and it explicitly recognises the territories and rights of Indigenous peoples and local communities for the first time. Compared with the earlier Aichi targets, 30x30 emphasises quality over raw area, since paper parks do not stop actual habitat loss.

绿色建筑到底“绿”在哪里？

What exactly makes a green building green?

绿色建筑在设计和运营中降低全生命周期环境影响：高性能围护结构减少冷暖能耗，高效暖通和LED降低用电，屋顶光伏和雨水收集就地利用资源，绿色建材减少隐含碳。绿色建筑评价体系把这些表现量化打分。建筑约占全球终端能耗三成，改造存量建筑同样潜力巨大。
Green buildings minimise environmental impact over their whole life: high-performance envelopes cut heating and cooling loads, efficient HVAC and LED lighting reduce electricity use, rooftop solar and rainwater harvesting tap local resources, and green materials lower embodied carbon. Rating systems such as green-building certification score these achievements. Buildings use roughly 30 percent of global final energy, so upgrading existing stock matters as much as new builds.

什么是生态补偿？它如何让保护者受益？

What are payments for ecosystem services (PES), and how do they benefit protectors?

生态补偿（PES）让生态服务的受益方向保护者付费：下游城市为上游水源涵养林付费，国家为退耕还林农户提供补贴，碳汇项目向森林所有者支付费用。它把生态保护的外部效益内部化，让“保护者受益、使用者付费”，弥补保护者放弃开发的机会成本，是许多国家协调发展与保护的关键制度。
Payments for ecosystem services make beneficiaries pay stewards: downstream cities pay for upstream watershed-protection forests, national programmes subsidise farmers who reforest cropland, and carbon projects pay forest owners. PES internalises the external benefits of conservation — protectors gain, users pay — offsetting the opportunity cost of forgoing development, and is a key instrument for balancing development and protection in many countries.

《巴塞尔公约》管的是什么？

What does the Basel Convention regulate?

《巴塞尔公约》管控有害废物的跨境转移，要求出口危险废料必须事先获得进口国同意，防止发达国家把污染转嫁到管理能力较弱的国家。它还推动废物减量和就近妥善处理。
The Basel Convention controls transboundary movements of hazardous waste, requiring prior consent from the importing country so wealthy nations cannot dump pollution on less-capable ones. It also promotes waste reduction and sound local treatment.

环境影响评价中的“公众参与”为什么重要？

Why does public participation matter in environmental impact assessment (EIA)?

环评要求项目公开信息、听取居民和专家意见，让受影响的社区有机会表达关切、提出替代方案，也促使建设单位修正设计、完善环保措施。有效的公众参与是项目环境风险的社会把关，符合“谁受影响、谁有发言权”的环境治理原则。
EIA requires publishing project information and hearing residents and experts, giving affected communities the chance to voice concerns and propose alternatives and pushing developers to revise designs and strengthen safeguards. Genuine public participation is a social gatekeeper for environmental risk, honouring the governance principle that those affected deserve a voice.

《京都议定书》与《巴黎协定》有何主要区别？

What are the main differences between the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement?

《京都议定书》以自上而下方式给少数发达国家设定强制减排目标，而《巴黎协定》采用各国自主贡献的普惠模式。巴黎协定覆盖范围更广，并把适应与资金纳入核心。它标志着气候治理从强制分配转向集体自主。
The Kyoto Protocol set binding targets for a limited group of developed countries in a top-down way, while the Paris Agreement uses nationally determined contributions for nearly all. Paris has broader coverage and puts adaptation and finance at its core. It marks a shift from imposed allocation to collective self-determination.

What are the goals of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?

这份2022年通过的框架被称为“自然版巴黎协定”。它的核心是“3030目标”：到2030年保护全球30%的陆地和海洋；还要求到2030年恢复至少30%的退化生态系统、减少污染、逐步取消危害自然的补贴。它把生物多样性保护与气候、粮食安全放在同一个盘子里统筹。
Adopted in 2022, this framework is often called the Paris Agreement for nature. Its centrepiece is the 30x30 target: protecting 30 percent of the world's land and ocean by 2030. It also commits to restoring at least 30 percent of degraded ecosystems, cutting pollution and phasing out subsidies harmful to nature by 2030 — tackling biodiversity, climate and food security together.

What is the difference between a carbon tax and carbon trading?

碳税直接规定每吨CO2的价格，排放成本可预测但总量不确定。碳交易固定总排放上限，总量可控但价格随市场波动。两者都是碳定价工具，常按国情组合使用。

什么是预防原则？

What is the precautionary principle?

预防原则主张：即使科学上尚未完全证明某种活动会造成严重危害，只要存在合理怀疑，就应采取预防措施避免潜在的环境或健康风险。它常用于化学品管理、转基因和气候变化等领域。这一原则强调“宁可谨慎，不可后悔”。
The precautionary principle holds that when an activity raises plausible threats of serious harm, lack of full scientific certainty should not delay preventive measures. It is used in chemicals management, GMOs, and climate policy. It emphasizes better safe than sorry.

什么是《联合国气候变化框架公约》（UNFCCC）？

What is the UNFCCC?

《联合国气候变化框架公约》是1992年通过、1994年生效的国际公约，确立了各国合作应对气候变化的基本框架与“共同但有区别的责任”原则。它下设的缔约方大会（COP）每年召开，催生了《京都议定书》和《巴黎协定》。几乎所有国家都是其缔约方。
The UNFCCC, adopted in 1992 and effective in 1994, sets the basic framework for international climate cooperation under the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. Its annual Conference of the Parties (COP) produced the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement. Nearly all nations are parties.

《巴黎协定》里的“国家自主贡献”（NDC）是什么？

What are Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement?

NDC 是各缔约方自己制定、定期更新并相互通报的减排与适应计划，体现“自下而上”的气候治理思路。协定要求各国每五年提交更有雄心的 NDC，并定期盘点总体进展。
An NDC is the emission-reduction and adaptation plan each party sets, updates and reports itself, reflecting a bottom-up approach to climate governance. The Agreement asks countries to submit ever more ambitious NDCs every five years and regularly take stock of collective progress.

小岛屿发展中国家面临哪些独特气候风险？

What unique climate risks do small island developing states face?

这些国家地势低平、国土狭小，海平面上升直接威胁国土淹没与淡水盐化。更强热带气旋与珊瑚退化还打击渔业与旅游业。它们排放极少却首当其冲，成为气候谈判中呼吁行动最有力的声音。
These nations are low-lying and small, so sea level rise directly threatens inundation and saltwater intrusion into freshwater. Stronger cyclones and coral decline also hit fisheries and tourism. They emit little yet are hit first, making them the most vocal calls for action in negotiations.

从环境史的角度看,1952年伦敦烟雾事件为什么会成为现代空气污染治理的分水岭?

Through the lens of environmental history, why did the Great Smog of London in 1952 become a watershed in modern air pollution control?

高压反气旋形成的逆温层使燃煤烟气在城市上空滞留数日,事后流行病学回溯估算超额死亡约一万两千人,远超当时的官方统计。事件直接促成1956年《清洁空气法》,家庭取暖逐步告别烟煤、转向无烟燃料和天然气,并开创了“烟雾本身即立法对象”的治理先例。公共卫生监测自此与大气化学研究深度结合,为后来酸雨与光化学烟雾的治理提供了方法范本。
A temperature inversion under a stagnant anticyclone held coal smoke over the city for days; retrospective epidemiology estimates some twelve thousand excess deaths, far beyond contemporary official counts. The catastrophe produced Britain's Clean Air Act of 1956, pushed domestic heating off raw coal onto smokeless fuels and gas, and established the precedent that visible smog itself can be made a statutory target. Public-health surveillance and atmospheric chemistry have been intertwined ever since, supplying the methodological template for later campaigns against acid rain and photochemical smog.

环境影响评价的“减缓层级”为何要求优先“避免”，而把“抵消补偿”放在最后？

Why does the mitigation hierarchy in EIA demand avoidance first and reserve biodiversity offsetting for last?

减缓层级按“避免—减量—修复—抵消”排序，体现生态损失可替代性递增：让工程避开敏感栖息地，损害根本不发生；技术措施只能缩小损害；事后修复难以复原原有物种组成与生态功能；抵消则是在别处重建同类生境，存在时间滞后与失败风险。把最不确定的手段放在末位，防止以纸面补偿掩盖原位的不可逆损失，从而实现净零损失。
The mitigation hierarchy ranks measures as avoid, minimise, restore and offset, mirroring the increasing substitutability of ecological losses. Steering a project away from sensitive habitat prevents damage outright; engineering controls merely shrink it; restoration afterwards can hardly recreate the original species composition and function; and offsets rebuild similar habitat elsewhere, with time lags and failure risks. Placing the least certain instrument last stops paper compensation from masking irreversible on-site losses and serves the goal of no net loss.

一条河既不会说话也不会签字,法律上谁有资格替它打官司?

A river can neither speak nor sign papers — who may sue on its behalf in court?

这是自然体权利的前沿问题。1972年斯通提出树木应有法律主体地位的设想后,进展走向判例:2017年新西兰立法授予旺格努伊河法人地位,由毛利部落与政府组成的监护人代其表达意愿;印度北阿坎德邦法院一度宣布恒河为「活人实体」;中国则走公益诉讼路径——环境保护法第五十八条允许符合条件的社会组织起诉污染者,检察机关亦能提起。核心难题始终是:代理人如何忠实翻译难以人类化的生态利益。
This is the frontier question of environmental law on the rights of nature. After Stone's 1972 thought experiment on trees having standing, practice caught up: New Zealand granted the Whanganui River legal personhood in 2017, with Maori and government guardians speaking for it; an Indian court briefly declared the Ganges a living entity; China takes a public-interest litigation path — Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law lets qualified social organizations sue polluters, and the procuratorate may also bring public-interest suits. The enduring puzzle: how representatives faithfully translate ecological interests that resist human framing.

巴黎协定的核心机制是什么？它为什么被称为“自下而上”的协议？

What are the core mechanisms of the Paris Agreement, and why is it called a bottom-up accord?

巴黎协定把全球升温控制在远低于2°C、并努力限制在1.5°C写为目标，但不再强制分配减排指标，而是由各国自行提出“国家自主贡献”（NDC）并定期更新，每五年开展一次“全球盘点”评估集体进展。它同时要求发达国家提供资金技术援助，构成了一个有弹性、能不断加码的全球气候治理框架。
The Paris Agreement commits the world to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C, but it does not impose national targets from above. Instead every country submits its own Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and updates it regularly, while a five-yearly global stocktake assesses collective progress. Developed countries also pledge finance and technology support — a flexible framework that can be ratcheted up over time.

什么是气候适应性（适应）？

What is climate adaptation?

适应指调整自然或人类系统以应对实际或预期气候影响、降低脆弱性。例子包括加固堤坝、培育耐旱作物和改进城市排水。与减排互补，适应在升温已无法避免时尤为关键。
Adaptation means adjusting natural or human systems to cope with actual or expected climate impacts and reduce vulnerability. Examples include strengthening dikes, breeding drought-resistant crops, and improving urban drainage. Complementing mitigation, adaptation is crucial where warming is already unavoidable.

CITES 是如何保护野生动物的？

How does CITES protect wildlife?

CITES（濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约）通过给物种分级、对跨境贸易发放许可，来防止过度国际贸易导致物种濒危。它不取代各国国内的保护法律，而是管住“国与国之间”的买卖。
CITES (the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) grades species and issues permits for cross-border trade to stop over-commercialization from driving them endangered. It does not replace national laws but regulates trade between countries.

什么是净零排放？

What does net-zero emissions mean?

净零指人为温室气体排放与通过自然或技术手段移除的排放量相抵消，使净增加为零。它不同于彻底不排放，而是排放等于移除的平衡。实现净零是《巴黎协定》长期目标的核心。
Net zero means human-caused greenhouse gas emissions are balanced by removals through natural or technological means, so the net addition is zero. It differs from zero emissions entirely; it is a balance of emit and remove. Achieving net zero is central to the Paris Agreement's long-term goal.

《蒙特利尔议定书》保护的是什么？

What does the Montreal Protocol protect?

《蒙特利尔议定书》于 1987 年达成，目标是逐步淘汰消耗臭氧层的氟氯碳化物（CFCs）等物质，保护平流层臭氧层。它被广泛视为最成功的国际环境条约，近年还追加了限制强效温室气体 HFCs 的《基加利修正案》。
The 1987 Montreal Protocol aims to phase out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs to protect the stratospheric ozone layer. It is widely seen as the most successful environmental treaty, and later added the Kigali Amendment to curb potent HFC greenhouse gases.

《巴黎协定》是什么？

What is the Paris Agreement?

《巴黎协定》是2015年达成的全球气候条约，目标是把升温控制在远低于2℃、努力限于1.5℃。各国自主提交减排贡献（NDC），并每五年更新加强。它是首个几乎覆盖所有国家的气候治理框架。
The Paris Agreement is a global climate treaty adopted in 2015 aiming to keep warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C. Countries submit their own emission-reduction contributions (NDCs), revised and strengthened every five years. It is the first climate governance framework covering nearly all nations.

什么是“世界地球日”？

What is Earth Day?

世界地球日是每年4月22日呼吁人们关注和保护环境的节日，1970年起源于美国，现已在各国广泛开展。这一天人们会参加清洁活动、植树和环保宣传。它提升了公众对污染和生态保护的意识。
Earth Day is observed every April 22 to promote environmental protection; it began in the United States in 1970 and is now marked worldwide. People join cleanups, tree planting, and awareness campaigns. It raised public awareness of pollution and conservation.

什么是环境影响评价？

What is an environmental impact assessment (EIA)?

环境影响评价是在修路、建厂等大型项目开工前，系统分析其可能对环境造成的影响，并提出减缓措施的程序。它能帮助决策者提前避免污染和生态破坏。许多国家把环评作为项目获批的必要条件。
An environmental impact assessment systematically analyzes a project's potential environmental effects—like a road or factory—before it starts, and proposes mitigation. It helps decision-makers avoid pollution and ecological harm in advance. Many countries require EIA for project approval.

什么是碳定价？

What is carbon pricing?

碳定价是对温室气体排放设定货币成本的政策，使污染者为其排放付费。常见形式包括碳税和碳排放交易体系。它的目的是用市场信号激励减排。
Carbon pricing is a policy that assigns a monetary cost to greenhouse gas emissions so polluters pay for what they emit. Common forms are carbon taxes and emissions trading systems. Its aim is to use market signals to incentivize reductions.

IPCC是做什么的？

What does the IPCC do?

IPCC即政府间气候变化专门委员会，负责评估全球气候变化的最新科学、影响与对策。它本身不做新研究，而是综合数千篇论文为各国政府提供权威报告。这些报告是气候谈判的关键科学依据。
The IPCC, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, assesses the latest science, impacts, and responses to climate change. It does not conduct new research but synthesizes thousands of papers into authoritative reports for governments. These reports are a key scientific basis for climate negotiations.
